source_text.body:
Research your family tree with Claude Code
The author used Claude Code to do genealogical research and map out multiple branches of their family tree using digitized records.
·
Nov 22, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
Brendan Nyhan ran Claude Code, using Opus 5.5 on Extra, to research his family tree. It drew on genealogical information that has been digitized and put online. He used it to map out several branches of the family. The post gives no detail on prompts, sources or his own checking.
How it went
He called the research incredible and was surprised by how much had been digitized. The post gives no figures, such as how many people or generations were found, and doesn't say how accurate the results were.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I want to research my family tree starting with [your name, birth year, and what you know about parents and grandparents, including places and approximate dates]. Search freely available digitized records such as [FamilySearch, national archives, census or immigration databases] and build a folder of notes with one file per person, citing the source for every fact. Mark anything uncertain as unverified rather than guessing, and finish with a summary file mapping each branch and listing the best next gaps to research.
Original source: https://bsky.app/profile/brendannyhan.bsky.social/post/3n2wi4awohc23
